backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so grad accumulation halves). In a fixed 300s budget with a small model, more optimizer steps usually beat larger batches.

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (accumulation steps 1 or less; ensure divisibility with seq len). Optionally scale MATRIX_LR by ~0.8 to compensate for the noisier gradient.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**17

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 so more of the time budget is spent at full LR.
backlog.title: Shorter warmdown

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 to anneal over most of the run.

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so that the LR does not drop fully to zero at the end of warmdown.

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.02 to soften the initial Muon and Adam steps.
backlog.title: Short warmup

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 384 at ASPECT_RATIO 64). A smaller model sees more tokens in 300s; check that dim stays divisible by HEAD_DIM, otherwise adjust ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so dim=512 rounds to a multiple of 128.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-per-time

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO 51 so that dim is about 512 (multiple of HEAD_DIM). Tests whether a deeper, narrower model wins at this budget. Reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 if OOM.
backlog.title: Depth 10 model

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to get more attention heads. Check that flash attention still works with that head dim.
backlog.title: HEAD_DIM 64

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSSL" or "SSL". Try "SL" first to test alternating windows. Only the pattern string changes.
backlog.title: All-short window pattern with final long

backlog.spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.05 for Muon.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.4 for the token embeddings.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Set SCALAR_LR = 0.25 to calm the per-layer scalar updates.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1 for Muon cautious decay.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Make the Muon weight decay scale with the LR multiplier (or linearly to 0 over training) rather than a constant, so the decay fades during warmdown.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decayed to zero

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.99) for a smoother second-moment estimate.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule: ramp from 0.85 to 0.97 over the first 300 steps, then hold at 0.97 for the middle of training and drop to 0.9 in warmdown. Edit only the momentum schedule function.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup tweak

backlog.spec: Reduce the logit softcap value (e.g. 15 to 10, or if it is 30, to 15) in the forward pass where tanh capping is applied.
backlog.title: Logit soft-cap lower

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with a gated SiLU unit, using hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64 so the parameter count is similar to the 4x MLP.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 to SwiGLU-style MLP

backlog.spec: If value embeddings exist on alternating layers, add them to every layer, or remove them if they are in all layers. Only the layer-selection predicate changes. Watch VRAM.
backlog.title: Untie value-embedding layers

backlog.spec: Multiply q and k after RMS norm by a learnable per-head scalar initialised at 1.2, or if one already exists, raise the fixed scale. This sharpens attention early.
backlog.title: QK-norm scale and init tweak

backlog.spec: Change the initial values of per-layer resid_lambdas from 1.0 to 0.9 and x0_lambdas from 0.1 to 0.2, so that the skip from the initial embedding is stronger.
backlog.title: Residual lambda init

backlog.spec: Make sure the attention output and MLP down projections are initialised to zero, or scale them by 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) if not.
backlog.title: Zero-init output projections check

backlog.spec: Remove any per-step .item() sync or logging in the training loop (log the loss only every 20 steps) so that more steps fit in the 300s. Do not touch the evaluation call.
backlog.title: Disable torch.compile dynamic overhead via larger eval-free loop

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step, applied once after accumulation.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: lr_mult = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress_in_warmdown)) (floored at FINAL_LR_FRAC). Edit only the schedule function.
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped warmdown

backlog.spec: Reduce the token embedding init std from 1.0 to 0.5 (and keep the lm_head init unchanged). This is a one-line change in init_weights.
backlog.title: Vocab-embedding init std lower

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**17 so that with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and sequence length 2048 there is a single micro-step per optimizer step (no gradient accumulation). Halving to 2**18 gave a big gain, so more steps should help again. If the code asserts divisibility, make sure TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is a multiple of DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN. Leave all learning rates unchanged.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17 with grad accum 1

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 4 and ASPECT_RATIO to 128 so model_dim is 512 (4 heads of dim 128). This is fewer layers but wider, so each step is cheaper and the GPU is used efficiently. Keep all other hyperparameters as they are. If the window pattern string is shorter than the depth, make sure the last layer remains full attention.
backlog.title: Depth 4 with wider model

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 to full over the first 2% of the time budget. With smaller batches and higher step counts, early instability at full LR may cost a little. Check that get_lr_multiplier handles warmup progress correctly (progress/WARMUP_RATIO) and leave warmdown unchanged.
backlog.title: Short linear LR warmup

backlog.spec: Make Muon's cautious weight decay follow the training progress: wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress) where progress is the time fraction elapsed, updated every step in the same place where the LR and momentum schedules are updated. Keep the initial WEIGHT_DECAY at 0.2. Strong decay early and none at the end is meant to help the final fit.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decayed to zero

backlog.spec: Set MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06. The batch size was halved and the model is smaller, so the Muon optimum may have moved. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.06 for smaller batch

backlog.spec: In the forward pass, find the logit soft-capping constant (likely 15 in softcap * tanh(logits/softcap)) and set it to 10. This mildly regularizes the output distribution and can stabilize training at high LR. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Lower logit soft-cap to 10

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSSL" or equivalently make all layers short except the last, which stays full attention. With DEPTH 6 this means 5 sliding-window layers and one full layer. This reduces attention compute per step, giving more steps in 300 s. Make sure the final layer is always forced to full context as the existing code does.
backlog.title: Short-window pattern with final long layer

backlog.spec: In init_weights, change the initial values of the per-layer residual scalars: set resid_lambdas to 0.9 (from 1.0) and x0_lambdas to 0.2 (from the current value, likely 0.1). This changes how much of the original embedding is mixed into each layer. Smaller models often benefit from a stronger skip to the input embedding. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Residual lambda init 0.9 / x0 lambda 0.2

backlog.spec: Change EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 together. The smaller batch gives noisier gradients so a lower embedding LR may help, while the lm_head is probably under-trained at 0.004. Both are Adam groups, so no other code changes are needed.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.3 and unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Where the model is wrapped with torch.compile, pass mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs". Compile time is not counted in the 300 s, but the startup plus training must stay under 450 s, so check that compile time stays moderate. It may produce faster kernels, giving more steps in the fixed time budget. Do not change the model math.
backlog.title: Compile with max-autotune-no-cudagraphs

memo:
Helped: cutting compute per step so the fixed 300 s buys more steps. DEPTH 6 (slot 4) scored 1.0829 and 1.0825, delta -0.0318. Halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (slot 10) scored 1.0655 and 1.0652, delta -0.0173. It is the incumbent at mean 1.0654. Both accepts carry a tripwire flag. Find out what it means before building on them.

Did not help: schedule tweaks (cosine warmdown +0.0030, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 +0.0031, 0.3 +0.0006), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0122), SwiGLU (+0.0038), gradient clipping (+0.0002), Adam betas (+0.0014). Small gains, all single runs and possibly noise: value embeddings on every layer (-0.0050), momentum schedule (-0.0006), FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.05 (-0.0007), weight decay 0.1 (-0.0001).

Next: check the tripwire first. Then try DEPTH 5 or 4 and a batch of 2**17. Retune the learning rate for the smaller model and batch. Replicate the value-embedding change on the new incumbent, and retry the loss-sync change. Avoid more schedule tweaks.
